meaning: The number 85 has no widely established symbolic meaning, but appears in two notable biblical events: Caleb's age when he received his inheritance, and the number of priests killed at Nob.
description: The number 85 is rarely mentioned with specific symbolic weight in the Bible or in Jewish numerology, but it appears in two notable biblical contexts. Caleb was 85 years old when he received his inheritance in the promised land (Joshua 14:10), after faithfully waiting 45 years for the fulfillment of God's promise. His advanced age underscores faithfulness and perseverance in faith – he was still as strong as when Moses first sent him out as a spy. In a darker context, 1 Samuel 22:18 tells how Doeg the Edomite killed 85 priests at Nob on King Saul's command, because they had helped David. This event is considered one of the most tragic during Saul's reign and marks a deep fall for the kingdom. Beyond these historical references, the number 85 is not attributed with any broad symbolic meaning in biblical tradition.

It is known that Caleb was 85 years old when he received his inheritance in the Promised Land (Joshua 14:10), which some interpret as a symbol of faithfulness and perseverance in faith. In Jewish tradition (Pirkei Avot 5:21), 80 years is mentioned as the age for strength, but 85 does not have its own established symbolic role. footnotes.text: In Pirkei Avot 5:21, 80 years is mentioned as the age for strength (gevura). Caleb's vitality at 85 can be seen in light of this tradition – he even surpassed that rabbinic milestone for strength.

According to rabbinic tradition (Talmud, Sanhedrin 95b), the massacre at Nob was regarded as a particularly grave sin, and Saul's treatment of the priestly city had far-reaching consequences for his dynasty.
